questions.q: You want to know whether customers who place more orders also spend more. Which chart fits best?
options: Pie chart
Line chart of average order count
Scatter plot of orders against spend
Stacked bar chart of regions
questions.explain: A relationship between two numeric variables is best shown with a scatter plot.

questions.q: Which chart is the natural choice for showing how monthly revenue changed across a year?
options: Line chart with months in order on the x-axis
Pie chart with a slice per month
Histogram of revenue
Scatter plot of region against month
questions.explain: Trends over time are shown with a line chart: time runs left to right and the joined points show direction and pace.

questions.q: Why are bar charts the workhorse for comparing categories?
options: They always use fewer colors than other charts
They can display more than a hundred categories clearly
They automatically sort the categories
People compare lengths from a common baseline accurately
questions.explain: Humans judge lengths along a shared baseline much more accurately than angles or areas.

questions.q: What does the histogram of customer spend in this lesson show?
options: Spend is right-skewed, with most customers in the low hundreds and a long tail of big spenders
Spend is perfectly symmetric around the average
Every segment spends exactly the same
Spend and orders are unrelated
questions.explain: The histogram shows the distribution of one variable: a bulk of customers at the lower end and a long right tail.

questions.q: Why is joining regions (North, South, East, West) with a line a poor choice?
options: Lines cannot be drawn in matplotlib
A line implies order and continuity that unrelated categories do not have
Lines are only for histograms
Regions must always be shown in a pie chart
questions.explain: A line connects points in an order and suggests values in between; categories like regions have no such progression, so use bars.
